title: Proactive tenant siphon & rebalance playbook to prevent GPU queue runaway
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After a hosted API incident on 2026-02-25 where a sudden tenant hotspot produced runaway queue buildup and delayed autoscaling, we need a coordinated program to proactively siphon low-priority tenant work, rebalance allocations, and validate safe eviction/soft-drain strategies. This ticket collects concrete action items: new telemetry anchors, an eviction simulator, tenant siphon policy, rebalance controller RFC, KV-cache priority heuristics, and controlled rollout steps for Experimentation and Canary fleets.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Incident review: total GPU saturation lasted ~42 minutes; 95th percentile latency spiked 5x. Root cause: tenant A caused sustained long-sequence generation that exhausted pool slots; autoscaler reacted after 9 minutes due to conservative hysteresis.

2026-03-04 — Design decision: prefer soft-siphon (defer non-critical prefetches and redirect to burst pool) vs hard-eviction to avoid poor customer UX. PM Priya Shah prefers soft approach unless SLA violations persist.

2026-03-08 — Eng review: Liam implemented a prototype eviction-simulator that replays queue traces against admission policy variants; initial results show soft-siphon reduces tail by ~35% with <0.5% request rejection.

2026-03-10 — Security review: no customer data exfiltration risk identified; eviction simulator runs on anonymized traces. Security owner Marcus Li flagged need for KMS key handling in any persisted telemetry.
2026-03-14 — QA: Canary rollout plan drafted. Need infra approval for burst-pool capacity before scheduled canary.
action_items: Telemetry: Add 'siphon_score' and 'queue_growth_rate' anchors to tenant-level telemetry (owner: Priya Shah; estimate: 3)
Eviction simulator: Generalize prototype to run on production-week-of traces and validate policies (owner: Liam O'Connor; estimate: 5)
Siphon policy RFC: Define thresholds, priority buckets, and fallback rules including burst-pool routing (owner: Ada Kim; estimate: 3)
Auto-scaler tuning: Reduce hysteresis window and add workload-aware priming for tenants above 90th percentile sustained usage (owner: Mateo Ruiz; estimate: 5)
KV-cache prioritization: Ensure hot prefixes for pinned tenants survive soft-siphon (owner: Jing Zhao; estimate: 2)
Runbook updates: Add automated playbook steps and escalation matrix (owner: Nandini Patel; estimate: 2)
Canary rollout: Schedule 2-phase canary and observability checks (owner: Liam O'Connor; estimate: 2)
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry anchors report in console and used by alerting within 2 weeks
Eviction simulator reproduces incident trace and outputs policy delta metrics (tail latency, rejected rate)
Siphon RFC approved by PM and Eng and merged to repo
Autoscaler config rolled to Canary fleet and shows <20% queue growth in 95th percentile within 1 week
Runbook includes automated remediation script and contact matrix
Canary rollout completes with <1% customer error increase and meets latency SLOs
